observations: Viewed all six Urus hero directions from final Art run: clear hood/carbon domains, open fascia apertures and louver depth, continuous side sculpture and curved glazing. Roof/interior/optics remain simplified.
Viewed current acceleration and open/locked climb captures; vehicle remains supported, visible obstacle contact retained, rubber confined to asphalt in acceleration fixture.

Viewed all thirteen final movement captures on three labelled sheets: seven terrain boundaries retain visible continuous driving/trails; six post-rise braking views show supported bodies. These endpoint stills complement the measured momentum/clearance checks and do not show every instant of suspension travel.

Viewed fourteen final transition directions on three labelled sheets: irregular, graded shoulders remain continuous without new hard seams or holes; paved edge stays narrower than natural soil/snow fringes. Remaining repetitive ground tiling is visible and not claimed solved.

Viewed all three fresh preset samples on one labelled sheet: same quarry scene retains body, terrain and opaque rock materials across settings. The frozen elevated camera/vehicle pose is a rendering sample, not hard-ground contact evidence; thermal scope comes from monitored short runs.

Actually viewed all 12 final controlled surface captures and four final real-driven mud/snow captures. They are fresh on the final code-stage executable and accepted unchanged material/art cook. Ruts101/101 passes.

Mud and snow actual drives each advance more than 32.8 feet without intervention, retain continuous depressions and avoid terrain/object body impacts. The trail images show low coherent grooves and side banks instead of the rejected deep alternating V/crater rows.

Snow floors are perceptibly pale blue-grey, with white banks and filtered tread detail. Mud shows damp brown floors with lower roughness. These remain physical height-field grooves with shading grain; individual grains, liquid flow and exact tire-lug collision are not simulated.

Firm dirt keeps a shallow light worn trail. Wet grass/loose dirt expose darker earth in loaded strips while retaining pressed green cover where the cut is shallow. Pale dry sand remains the most subtle of the six controlled surface views, with low rounded profiles and no black rubber ribbon.

The whole authored Winter Expedition landscape remains static; this excavation review concerns the native proving-ground surfaces. The focused straight tracks are inherently more uniform than a varying-load route. No production racing-game or surveyed snow-depth accuracy is claimed.
